violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.credit_accounts has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.credit_accounts FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY missing
violations.message: Table public.app_admins has RLS enabled but not FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. The table owner role still bypasses RLS, which often masks broken policies in development and CI. Run `ALTER TABLE public.app_admins FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;`.

violations.title: All policies on table are permissive
violations.message: Every policy on public.credit_accounts is permissive. Permissive policies combine with OR — adding one RESTRICTIVE policy gives a floor (e.g. tenant scoping) that no OR branch can bypass, for the roles in its own TO list. Use TO PUBLIC to bind every role: measured, a restrictive TO authenticated left authenticated at 1 row and another role at 3.

violations.title: RLS enabled but no policies defined
violations.message: Table public.app_admins has RLS enabled but no policies defined. Postgres treats this as deny-all for every role RLS applies to — such a query returns zero rows. The table owner still reads every row unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set, and a BYPASSRLS role or superuser reads it regardless. If that's intentional (e.g., a deny-by-default audit table), allowlist it in [lint.rules.SEC009]; otherwise add the policies the migration was meant to include.

violations.title: RLS-enabled table has no write-side policy
violations.message: Table public.credit_accounts has RLS enabled and 1 policy, but every policy is FOR SELECT — no policy covers INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE. With RLS enforced and no write-side policy, writes by non-owner roles are denied: INSERT raises a row-violates-policy error, while UPDATE and DELETE silently affect zero rows. If the table is meant to be read-only for these roles (writes done by a table-owning or BYPASSRLS role), allowlist it as 'public.credit_accounts' in [lint.rules.SEC022]. Otherwise add a policy covering the write commands — a FOR ALL policy, or a FOR INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE policy.

violations.title: Auth function called per-row in policy USING/WITH CHECK
violations.message: Policy 'see own balance' on public.credit_accounts calls an auth function in USING without wrapping it in a subquery. Postgres re-evaluates the call per row. Wrap as e.g. (SELECT auth.uid()) so the planner caches the result for the whole statement.
